findings.title: The NCAA Rule 7 scoring engine is fully built, sourced, tested - and wired to nothing
evidence: packages/core/src/lib/ncaaScoringRules.ts is 1401 lines: 14 meet formats, exhibition isolation (7-10-1), DQ place advancement (7-7), tie division (7-8), lost-place accounting, per-format maxScorersPerTeam.
tests/ncaaScoringRules.test.ts is 864 lines.
grep across the monorepo for every export returns exactly two consumers: its own test file and a re-export in packages/core/src/index.ts. Zero product code calls it.

The product scores via calculatePoints in packages/core/src/lib/utils.ts against the legacy ScoringSettings shape (consumers: scoringEngine, rosterOptimizer, arbitrage/*, scenarioDiff, matrix swimCloudMeetImportBridge).

Provenance verified this session: data/scoring_rules/sources/ncaascoring.pdf sha256 5b98f8f69470606ea179b053b86d7fb4451f61a874c0fff5d8d18b369d6bb92e is byte-identical to a fresh fetch of https://meets.swimdna.org/media/ncaascoring.pdf and matches the manifest.
findings.consequence: ScoringSettings models relay points as a scalar relayMultiplier. That is exactly correct for all six championship field sizes (relay table is 2x individual at 6/8/12/16/18/24 - all verified against the rulebook). It is structurally WRONG for every non-championship format: dual 6+ lanes is individual 9-4-3-2-1 with relays 11-4-2 (11 is not 2x9); dual <=5 lanes is 5-3-1 with relays 7 (7 is not 2x5). The three dual diving tables (7-1-4) are also inexpressible - diving is modelled only as diverScorerWeight, not as its own place-value table. A dual meet is the most common format in college swimming and the app cannot represent one today.

findings.title: Crawl resume is per-capture; the global page store is not consulted across meets
evidence: data/swimcloud-captures/pages/ is keyed GLOBALLY by canonicalUrl (123 files on disk), so page bytes are already shared across captures.

But crawler-content.ts readAlreadyCaptured() builds its skip set from a single SUBJECT's capture record (GET /api/swimcloud/captures/{id}), not from the global page store. A different meet re-fetches pages whose bytes are already on disk.
Page-kind breakdown of the real 234-page capture: swimmerTimes 184 (78.6%), meetTeamSwims 42 (17.9%), teamRoster 8 (3.4%).
A swimmer's personal-bests page is the SAME canonicalUrl regardless of which meet is being crawled, so it is the page kind that repeats most across a season's crawls.
Measured wall time: meetTeamSwims 42 pages/122s (2981ms gap), teamRoster 8 pages/21s (3002ms gap), swimmerTimes 184 pages/75s (409ms gap, pooled). Total ~218s for 4 teams.
findings.consequence: Two real speedups remain available WITHOUT touching the 3000ms floor the user ruled out (d3): (1) Job-scoped page selection - swimmerTimes is 78.6% of all pages fetched, and a meet-results-only job does not need any of them. (2) Cross-capture reuse - consult the global pages/ store when building the skip set, gated by a real freshness policy, since a personal-bests page legitimately changes as a swimmer races. The existing provisional/final cacheStatus is the right mechanism: a finished meet's pages are immutable and can be promoted to 'final'; provisional pages need a TTL. Both reduce traffic rather than increasing it.
findings.correctionNote: An earlier reading of this finding in the same session was WRONG and was corrected before any work was briefed on it. The wrong version said 'every page is provisional, so a re-crawl re-fetches everything'. That is false: extensions/swimcloud-companion/src/captureResume.ts implements a real, unit-tested, fail-safe resume, and re-crawling the SAME meet correctly skips pages already stored. The cacheStatus field belongs to the server-side Track B Playwright cache (packages/swimcloud/src/cache.ts), not to the extension's resume path. Recorded here so nobody re-derives the wrong conclusion from the raw cacheStatus counts.

findings.title: RESOLVED ALREADY - prelims/finals rounds are resolved from meetEvent pages
evidence: packages/matrix/src/lib/swimCloudMeetImportBridge.ts resolves a swim's round from /results/{meetId}/event/{n}/ pages, which print one caption-labelled table per round plus the real meet Score column. Its own comment: 'This is what turns "excluded as ambiguous" into "scored as the round it actually was".'

The eventResults option is genuinely supplied, not an optional-and-never-passed parameter: apps/shell/lib/swimcloudCaptureRoutes.ts parses them (line ~713/735) and packages/matrix/src/components/OpsModule.tsx:485 passes selection.eventResults into the bridge.

The crawl actually fetches them: crawler-content.ts runs runEventResultsPass (line ~922), planned by planEventResultsSteps -> planMeetEventResults, pooled at EVENT_RESULTS_CONCURRENCY=3 / EVENT_RESULTS_STAGGER_MS=400.

Exclusion via 'ambiguous-round-duplicate' still exists as the correct fallback for a swim whose event page is absent, did not parse, or carried no round caption - absence of data, never a guess. That is right and stays.
findings.consequence: The better a swimmer is, the more likely they vanish from an opponent-scouting import. Directly undermines user decision d1's scouting/projection requirement. Candidate fix: use meetEvent pages, which do carry round context, as a disambiguation SOURCE (not a guess).
findings.correctionNote: An earlier reading of this finding in the same session was WRONG. It was taken from plans/2026-09-10/01-SWIMCLOUD-SCORING-CORRECTNESS.md, which describes the problem and an interim fix that EXCLUDED ambiguous prelims/finals groups wholesale. A later change resolved it properly and the plan doc was never updated. Do not re-open this from that doc. Lesson recorded: verify a plan doc's claim against the code before briefing work on it - this repo's docs lag its code.
findings.consequenceForP3: Important knock-on for the crawl-speed work: the archived 234-page capture (2026-09-10) PREDATES the event-results pass and contains zero meetEvent pages. A crawl run today therefore fetches MORE pages than that sample - one meetEvent page per distinct event on top of the 234. The user's 'data pulling is very slow' impression is likely of a post-eventResults crawl, so the real current page count is higher than the measured baseline. Re-measure against a current crawl before claiming any speedup percentage.

Not re-exported from packages/core/src/index.ts.

findings.title: The event catalog is a fixed short-course-yards NCAA program
evidence: packages/core/src/lib/eventCatalog.ts hardcodes 17 INDIVIDUAL_EVENTS plus 2 relay-split events.

Consumers are 4 Manager UI components only (AthleteEntriesSection, AthleteHistorySection, AthleteCreditedSwimsRow, AthleteLineupEditorPanel) - it is an entry-planning picker list, not a scoring gate. Severity is bounded by that.
CONVERSION_FACTORS in constants.ts covers 400 Freestyle and 1500 Freestyle; INDIVIDUAL_EVENTS does not list 400 Freestyle at all.
findings.consequence: A coach planning a long-course or non-standard meet cannot pick an event the program actually contests - notably 400 Freestyle, which the conversion table already knows about. Relevant to the 'usable for all divisions/formats' requirement, but lower priority than scoring formats because it only limits the planning picker.

findings.title: Team colours and aliases hardcode four specific schools
evidence: packages/core/src/constants.ts TEAM_COLORS_MAP hardcodes Henderson State, Ouachita Baptist, Delta State, Oklahoma Baptist.
packages/core/src/data/teamAliases.ts hardcodes HSU/OBU/OUAC acronyms, though it also has a generic acronym builder that degrades gracefully for unknown schools.
findings.consequence: Cosmetic only - an unlisted school falls back to the NEON_COLORS rotation. Worth making user-editable eventually; not a blocker.

openDecisions.question: How should the Rule 7 engine (ncaaScoringRules.ts) and the legacy ScoringSettings converge?
openDecisions.optionA: Replace: make calculatePoints delegate to computeNcaaEventScoring. One engine, no duplication, every format correct by construction. But it rewrites the scoring data path that NSISC totals are byte-exact verified against, and that optimizer/arbitrage/scenario-diff all depend on. Highest risk before a deadline.
openDecisions.optionB: Extend: add optional relayPoints[] / divingPoints[] / per-team per-event place caps to ScoringSettings, and GENERATE the built-in presets from NCAA_FORMAT_RULESETS so the tables still live in exactly one place. calculatePoints keeps its structure and learns to prefer relayPoints over relayMultiplier when present. Additive, every existing verified behaviour preserved, every format expressible. Recommended.
openDecisions.recommendation: B, with A recorded as the longer-term convergence once the deadline passes.
